purpose: Diagnosis of the previous delivered artifact, not a post-release acceptance claim
finding: The original-path bootloader starts at Low integrity and cannot create a normal Medium-integrity runtime directory. The same executable bytes in a fresh copy start at Medium and succeed.

fresh_approved_matrix.execution: require_escalated; fresh fixture created by the launching context
fresh_approved_matrix.interpretation: The exact original path fails across tested cwd/TEMP/LOCALAPPDATA variations; a separate Unicode-path copy succeeds. This is not a general Unicode-path failure.

method: Matrix fixtures and copies were freshly created in the same approved caller context, avoiding reused sandbox-account fixture ownership as a confound.
API reports use Frida observations of newly spawned isolated owned processes. Arguments/results are observed, not replaced. Token measurements precede installation of observation hooks.
Every launch uses a private share, test profile, chat-data directory, LOCALAPPDATA, temporary directories, ephemeral port, offscreen Qt and owned kill-on-close process job.
No delivered binary bytes, real settings, chat data, registry, directory ACLs, global environment or pre-existing service were modified by diagnosis.
boundaries: Controlled process creation is not an Explorer double-click interaction. The approved ordinary matrix reproduces the native error at the original path.
API evidence is capped at 300 events and is not complete filesystem coverage. NtCreateFile return observation is not kernel tracing and cannot alone exclude deeper interception.
Earlier sandbox matrix and approved replay of sandbox-created fixtures are retained separately but are not the primary comparison evidence.
No claim is made that changing TEMP alone, requiring elevation or weakening directory permissions is a valid repair.

The inherited Low file-label observation and replacement are recorded separately in release-artifact.json. Final-path acceptance is recorded separately in startup-token-delivered.json and startup-temp-delivered.json.

official_references.relevance: Low cannot write Medium even when the DACL permits it; a new process receives the minimum of the caller and executable integrity levels.
ReplaceFileW preserves original destination attributes including its DACL; this is not the chosen replacement operation.
Same-volume moves normally preserve original permissions. The exact local os.replace behavior is verified by integrity-replace-probe.json rather than inferred for all SACL cases.
